 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of deconsolidation, we expect that our future merchant energy results will differ from historical results primarily due to the
following factors: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Revenues&#151;We
will sell between 85-90% of the output of CENG's plants, excluding output sold by CENG directly to third parties, rather than 100% of the plants'
total output including volumes contracted to third parties. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Fuel
and purchased energy expenses&#151;We will not include nuclear fuel expense but instead will reflect our purchase of between 85-90% of the output of CENG's
plants, excluding output sold directly to third parties, as provided under the terms of the PPA with CENG. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Operating
expenses&#151;We will no longer include CENG's plant operating costs or general and administrative expenses. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Depreciation
and amortization expense&#151;We will no longer include deprecation of CENG's nuclear plants. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally,
we will record our 50.01% share of CENG's financial results and amortization of the CENG basis difference in the "Equity Investment (Losses) Earnings" line in our
Consolidated Statements of Income (Loss). We discuss the accounting for our retained investment in CENG in more detail in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;2 to Consolidated Financial
Statements.</I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Revenues and Fuel and Purchased Energy Expenses  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our merchant energy business manages the revenues we realize from the sale of energy and energy-related products to our customers and our costs of
procuring fuel and energy. The difference between revenues and fuel and purchased energy expenses, including all direct expenses, represents the gross margin of our merchant energy business, and this
measure is a useful tool for assessing the profitability of our merchant energy business. Accordingly, we believe it is appropriate to discuss the operating results of our merchant energy business by
analyzing the changes in gross margin between periods. In managing our portfolio, we may terminate, restructure, or acquire contracts. Such transactions are within the normal course of managing our
portfolio and may materially impact the timing of our recognition of revenues, fuel and purchased energy expenses, and cash flows. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
the third quarter of 2007, we changed the management of the wholesale procurement function for retail gas activities from our Customer Supply operations to our Global Commodities
operation. In connection with this change, we began to prospectively account for the underlying retail gas contracts as derivative contracts subject to mark-to-market
accounting, under which changes in fair value are recorded in revenues as they occur. This activity was previously accounted for on a gross basis and recorded in accrual revenues and fuel and
purchased energy expenses. The change to
mark-to-market accounting for this activity reduced both our accrual revenues and fuel and purchased energy expenses in 2008 and 2007. However, the change had a minimal impact
on gross margin. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
discuss our merchant energy revenues, fuel and purchased energy expenses, and gross margin below. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>
<U>Gross Margin</U> </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>We
analyze our merchant energy gross margin in the following categories. </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Generation&#151;our
operation that owns, operates, and maintains fossil, nuclear (through November&nbsp;6, 2009), and renewable generating facilities and holds
indirect interests in nuclear generating facilities (since November&nbsp;6, 2009), qualifying facilities, and power projects in the United States. We present the gross margin results of this
operation based on a 100% hedged assumption for the portfolio, related to both output from the facilities and the fuel used to generate electricity. The assumption is based on executing hedges at
current market prices with the Global Commodities operation at the end of each prior fiscal year in order to ensure that the Generation operation is fully hedged. Therefore, all commodity price risk
is managed by and presented in the results of our Global Commodities operation as discussed below. Changes in gross margin of our Generation operation during the period are due to changes in the level
of output from the generating assets, and changes in gross margin between years are a result of changes in prices and expected output. Gross margin excludes our equity investment earnings from our
nuclear joint ventures, qualifying facilities, and power projects. We discuss our treatment of equity investment earnings in more detail in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;1 to Consolidated
Financial Statements</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Customer
Supply&#151;our load-serving operation that provides energy products and services to wholesale and retail electric and natural gas customers,
including distribution utilities, cooperatives, aggregators, and commercial, industrial and governmental customers. We present the gross margin results of this operation based on the gross margin
value of new customer supply arrangements at the time of execution assuming an estimated level of customer usage and the impact of any changes in the underlying usage of the customers based on actual
energy deliveries including decreased demand related to the current economic environment. Changes in estimated customer usage result from attrition (customers changing suppliers) or variable load risk
(changes in actual usage when compared to expected usage). All commodity price risk is presented in and managed by our Global Commodities operation. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Global
Commodities&#151;our marketing, risk management, and trading operation that manages contractually owned physical assets, including generation facilities and
natural gas properties, provides risk management services, and trades energy and energy-related commodities. This operation provides the wholesale risk management function for our Generation and
Customer Supply operations, as well as our structured products and energy investments portfolios, and includes our merchant energy business' actual hedged positions with third parties. Therefore,
changes in gross margin for this operation result mostly from changes in commodity prices and positions across the various commodities and regions in which we transact. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> <U>Generation</U>  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The $57&nbsp;million increase in Generation gross margin in 2009 compared to 2008 is primarily due to the following: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$178&nbsp;million
increase from higher energy prices for the output of our generating assets in the PJM and New York regions based on prices established at the end of 2008
(see Global Commodities discussion below for impact of price changes during 2009), and </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$130&nbsp;million
due to the timing and duration of planned and unplanned outages at our generating plants. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$210&nbsp;million

2010, our gross margin for Generation will be lower than in 2009 as a result of the sale of a 49.99% membership interest in CENG to EDF on November&nbsp;6, 2009. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> <U>Customer Supply</U>  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The $34&nbsp;million increase in Customer Supply gross margin in 2009 compared to 2008 is primarily due to the following: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$108&nbsp;million
of higher gross margin mostly related to the consolidation of a retail power supply variable interest entity for which we became the primary beneficiary
in December 2008 and consolidated, and </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$9&nbsp;million
of higher mark-to-market results primarily in our retail gas operation. We discuss these results in more detail in the </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><I>Mark-to-Market</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> section. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;These
increases were partially offset by the following: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$66&nbsp;million
of lower gross margin as a result of fewer customers and unfavorable variable load risk associated with wholesale and retail power primarily due to
variances from normal weather and lower demand resulting from the economic downturn and our efforts to reduce risk in the business, and </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$17&nbsp;million
related to lower realization of contracts executed in prior periods and lower volumes in our wholesale and retail power supply operations, partially
offset by higher margins on new business originated and realized during 2009. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
$124&nbsp;million decrease in Customer Supply gross margin in 2008 compared to 2007 is primarily due to the following: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$112&nbsp;million
of lower gross margin related to unfavorable price movements and lower volumes in our retail power operation, </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$49&nbsp;million
of lower gross margin related to lower realization of contracts executed in prior periods and lower new business originated and realized during the year
at our wholesale power operation, and </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$27&nbsp;million
of lower mark-to-market results in our retail gas operation. We discuss this in more detail in the </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><I>Mark-to-Market</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> section. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;These
decreases were partially offset by approximately $64&nbsp;million of higher gross margin related to our retail gas operation primarily due to the acquisition of Cornerstone
Energy on July&nbsp;1, 2007. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> <U>Global Commodities</U>  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>We analyze Global Commodities results in the following categories: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Portfolio
Management and Trading&#151;our centralized risk management service related to energy price risk associated with our generation fleet, wholesale and retail
customer supply business, and our structured products portfolio. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Structured
Products&#151;customized risk management products in the power, gas, coal and freight markets (e.g.,&nbsp;generation tolls, gas transport and storage,
and global coal and freight logistics). During 2009, we reduced our participation in the coal, freight and gas trading markets through the divestiture of our international coal and freight and our
natural gas trading businesses. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Energy
Investments&#151;investments in energy assets that primarily include natural gas properties and a joint interest in an entity that owns dry bulk cargo vessels.
We sold our interest in the entity that owns dry bulk cargo vessels during 2009. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
$30&nbsp;million decrease in gross margin from our Global Commodities operation during 2009 compared to the same period of 2008 is primarily due to: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$140&nbsp;million
of lower gross margin from our energy investments operation primarily related to lower business realized on our upstream gas activities within 2009, and </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$139&nbsp;million
of lower gross margin in our structured products portfolio primarily as a result of fewer transactions during 2009. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;These
decreases were partially offset by an increase of $249&nbsp;million in our portfolio management and trading operation. These changes are discussed further in the table below. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As
previously discussed, the energy markets were affected by substantial volatility in commodity prices during 2008. These market impacts are reflected in the $433&nbsp;million
decrease in gross margin from our Global Commodities operation during 2008 compared to the same period of 2007 primarily due to $698&nbsp;million of lower gross margin in our portfolio management
and trading activities, which are discussed further in the table below. This is partially offset by: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$208&nbsp;million
from gains in our structured products portfolio, consisting of approximately $135&nbsp;million as a result of the termination and sale of
in-the-money energy purchase contracts, coal supply contracts, and freight contracts to eliminate or reduce operation and performance risk with certain counterparties, and
approximately $73&nbsp;million related to higher realization of contracts executed in prior periods, and </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$57&nbsp;million
in our energy investments operation primarily due to higher realization of contracts executed in prior periods. </FONT></DD></DL>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Mark-to-Market  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Mark-to-market results include net gains and losses from origination, risk management, and trading activities for which we
use the mark-to-market method of accounting. We discuss these activities and the mark-to-market method of accounting in more detail in the </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><I>Critical Accounting Policies</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> section and in </FONT><FONT
SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;1 to Consolidated Financial Statements</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
nature of our operations and the use of mark-to-market accounting for certain activities create fluctuations in mark-to-market
earnings. We cannot predict these fluctuations, but the impact on our earnings could be material. We discuss our market risk in more detail in the </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Risk
Management</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> section. The primary factors that cause fluctuations in our mark-to-market results are: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>changes
in the level and volatility of forward commodity prices and interest rates, </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>counterparty
creditworthiness, </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>the
number and size of our open derivative positions, and </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>the
number, size, and profitability of new transactions, including termination or restructuring of existing contracts. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
2009, we focused our activities on reducing capital requirements, reducing long-term economic risk, and reducing short- and interim-term liquidity
requirements. These actions may impact the future results of the merchant energy business, particularly the size of and potential for changes in fair value of activities subject to
mark-to-market accounting. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
primary components of mark-to-market results are origination gains and gains and losses from risk management and trading activities. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Origination
gains arise primarily from contracts that our Global Commodities operation structures to meet the risk management needs of our customers or relate to our trading activities.
Transactions that result in origination gains may be unique and provide the potential for individually significant revenues and gains from a single transaction. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Risk
management and trading&#151;mark-to-market represents both realized and unrealized gains and losses from changes in the value of our portfolio,
including the effects of changes in valuation adjustments. In addition to our fundamental risk management and trading activities, we also use non-trading derivative contracts subject to
mark-to-market accounting to manage our exposure to changes in market prices, while in general the underlying physical transactions related to these activities are accounted
for on an accrual basis. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
discuss the changes in mark-to-market results below. We show the relationship between our mark-to-market results and the change in our
net mark-to-market energy asset later in this section. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Mark-to-market
results were as follows: </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
HREF="#bg49001a_main_toc">Table of Contents</A></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Total mark-to-market results decreased $445.9&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2009 compared to
the same period of 2008. The period-to-period variance in unrealized changes in fair value was due to decreased unrealized risk management and trading results of
$372.1&nbsp;million and the decrease in origination gains of $73.8&nbsp;million. We discuss the decrease in origination gains below. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
decrease in risk management and trading results of $372.1&nbsp;million was primarily due to: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$203&nbsp;million
of lower results in our domestic coal portfolio primarily as a result of less favorable price movements relating to economic hedges which substantially
decreased in value as coal prices decreased in 2009, </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$104&nbsp;million
of lower gains in our international coal and freight operation as a result of its divestiture in March 2009, </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$123&nbsp;million
of lower gains in our wholesale natural gas risk management and trading operation primarily as a result of the divestiture of our natural gas trading
operation in the beginning of April 2009, and </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$45&nbsp;million
of lower results related to our emissions trading activities primarily as a result of a less favorable price environment. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;These
decreases were partially offset by the following: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$84&nbsp;million
of higher results on open positions primarily due to the absence of losses in our power and transmission risk management activities primarily in the PJM,
Northeast, and New York regions as a result of a more favorable price environment in 2009 and our activities to reduce risk and improve liquidity, and </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$19&nbsp;million
of lower losses in our retail gas portfolio primarily due to a more favorable price environment in 2009. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Total
mark-to-market results decreased $309.1&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2008 compared to the same period of 2007 primarily due to
unrealized changes in fair value. The period-to-period variance in unrealized changes in fair value was due to lower gains from unrealized changes in fair value of
$341.0&nbsp;million from risk management and trading, partially offset by an increase in origination gains of $31.9&nbsp;million. We discuss the increase in origination gains below. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
net decrease in risk management and trading gains of $341.0&nbsp;million was primarily due to: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$619&nbsp;million
of increased losses primarily related to power and transmission trading activities in the northeast, PJM, and ERCOT regions due to unfavorable price
movements, execution of transactions to reduce our risk position consistent with changes in our strategy, and execution of those transactions in less liquid market conditions, </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>lower
gains of $29&nbsp;million from our emissions trading activities due primarily to unfavorable price movements, and </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$104&nbsp;million
of increased losses related to unfavorable price movements on certain economic hedges of accrual transactions, primarily related to gas transportation
and storage and freight activities that do not qualify for or are not designated as cash-flow hedges. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
risk management and trading results were partially offset by: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$356&nbsp;million
of gains primarily as a result of favorable price movements relating to economic hedges which substantially increased in value as coal prices decreased
in the fourth quarter of 2008. These positions were previously accounted for as cash-flow hedges and were de-designated due to the announced sale of our international
commodities operation, and </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>$55&nbsp;million
of gains primarily related to our wholesale and retail gas businesses due to favorable price movements on our sales of wholesale and retail natural gas. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
did not record any origination gains during 2009. During 2008, our Global Commodities operation amended certain nonderivative contracts to mitigate counterparty performance risk under
the existing contracts. As a result of these amendments, the revised contracts became derivatives subject to mark-to-market accounting. The change in accounting for these
contracts from nonderivative to derivative resulted in substantially all of the origination gains for 2008 presented in the unrealized mark-to-market results table above. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
2007, our Global Commodities operation amended certain nonderivative power sales contracts such that the new contracts became derivatives subject to
mark-to-market accounting. Simultaneous with the amending of the nonderivative contracts, we executed at current market prices several new offsetting derivative power purchase
contracts subject to mark-to-market accounting. The combination of these transactions resulted in substantially all of the origination gains presented for 2007 in the preceding
table, as well as mitigated our risk exposure under the amended contracts. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
origination gains in 2007 from these transactions was partially offset by approximately $12&nbsp;million of losses in our accrual portfolio due to the reclassification of losses
related to cash-flow hedges previously established for the amended nonderivative contracts from "Accumulated other comprehensive loss" into earnings. In the absence of these transactions,
the economic value represented by the origination gains and the losses associated with cash-flow hedges would have been recognized over the remaining term of the contracts, which extended
through the first quarter of 2009. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
recognition of origination gains is generally dependent on sufficient available market data that validates the initial fair value of the contract. Liquidity and market conditions
impact our ability to identify sufficient, objective market price information to permit recognition of origination gains. As a result, the level of origination gains we are able to recognize may vary
from year to year as a result of the number, size, and market price transparency of the individual transactions executed in any period. </FONT></P>

 </DIV>
 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As discussed in our </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Critical Accounting Policies</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> section, our "Derivative assets and liabilities"
include contracts accounted for as hedges and those accounted for on a mark-to-market basis. These amounts are presented in our Consolidated Balance Sheets after the impact of
netting, which is discussed in more detail in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;1 to Consolidated Financial Statements</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. Due to the impacts of commodity prices, the number of
open positions, master netting arrangements, and offsetting risk positions on the presentation of our derivative assets and liabilities in our Consolidated Balance Sheets, we believe an evaluation of
the net position is the most relevant measure, and is discussed in more detail below. However, we present our gross derivatives in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;13 to Consolidated Financial
Statements.</I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
decrease of $1,246.6&nbsp;million in our net derivative liability subject to hedge accounting since December&nbsp;31, 2008 primarily was due to $1,896&nbsp;million of
realization of out-of-the-money cash-flow hedges at the time the forecasted transaction occurred, partially offset by $649&nbsp;million of increased
unrealized losses on our remaining out-of-the-money cash-flow hedge positions primarily related to decreases in power, natural gas, and coal prices
during 2009. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
following are the primary sources of the change in our net derivative asset subject to mark-to-market accounting during 2009 and 2008: </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes in our net derivative asset subject to mark-to-market accounting that affected earnings were as follows: </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Origination
gains represent the initial unrealized fair value at the time these contracts are executed to the extent permitted by applicable accounting rules. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Unrealized
changes in fair value represent unrealized changes in commodity prices, the volatility of options on commodities, the time value of options, and other valuation
adjustments. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Changes
in valuation techniques represent improvements in estimation techniques, including modeling and other statistical enhancements used to value our portfolio to more
accurately reflect the economic value of our contracts. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Reclassification
of settled contracts to realized represents the portion of previously unrealized amounts settled during the period and recorded as realized revenues. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
net derivative asset also changed due to the following items recorded in accounts other than in our Consolidated Statements of Income (Loss): </FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Changes
in value of exchange-listed futures and options are adjustments to remove unrealized revenue from exchange-traded contracts that are included in nonregulated
revenues. The fair value of these contracts is recorded in "Accounts receivable" rather than "Derivative assets" in our Consolidated Balance Sheets because these amounts are settled through our margin
account with a third party broker. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Net
changes in premiums on options reflects the accounting for premiums on options purchased as an increase in the net derivative asset and premiums on options sold as a
decrease in the net derivative asset. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Contracts
acquired represents the initial fair value of acquired derivative contracts recorded in "Derivative assets and liabilities" in our Consolidated Balance Sheets.
Substantially all of this activity for 2009 related to the divestiture of our international commodities operation, Houston-based gas trading operation, and certain other trading operations in order to
transfer risk and reward to the buyers. </FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Dedesignated

treatment, transfers of derivative contracts from mark-to-market treatment to cash-flow hedges, and those derivative contracts that did not meet the qualifications
of cash flow hedge accounting. During 2009, substantially all of the activity related to dedesignations in connection with the strategic objective of restructuring and reducing the risk of our
portfolio. </FONT></DD></DL>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Management uses its best estimates to determine the fair value of commodity and derivative contracts it holds and sells. These estimates consider
various factors including closing exchange and over-the-counter price quotations, time value, volatility factors, and credit exposure. Additionally, because the depth and
liquidity of the power markets varies substantially between regions and time periods, the prices used to determine fair value could be affected significantly by the volume of transactions executed.
Future market prices and actual quantities will vary from those used in recording mark-to-market energy assets and liabilities, and it is possible that such variations could be
material. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
manage our mark-to-market risk on a portfolio basis based upon the delivery period of our contracts and the individual components of the risks within each
contract. Accordingly, we manage the energy purchase and sale obligations under our contracts in separate components based upon the commodity (e.g.,&nbsp;electricity or gas), the product
(e.g.,&nbsp;electricity for delivery during peak or off-peak hours), the delivery location (e.g.,&nbsp;by region), the risk profile (e.g.,&nbsp;forward or option), and the delivery
period (e.g.,&nbsp;by month and year). </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
electricity, fuel, and other energy contracts we hold have varying terms to maturity, ranging from contracts for delivery the next hour to contracts with terms of ten years or more.
Because an active, liquid electricity futures market comparable to that for other commodities has not developed, many contracts are direct contracts between market participants and are not
exchange-traded or financially settling contracts that can be readily offset in their entirety through an exchange or other market mechanism. Consequently, we and other market participants generally
realize the value of these contracts as cash flows become due or payable under the terms of the contracts rather than through selling or liquidating the contracts themselves. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
order to realize the entire value of a long-term contract in a single transaction, we would need to sell or assign the entire contract. If we were to sell or assign any of
our long-term contracts in their entirety, we may not realize the entire value reflected in the preceding table. However, based upon the nature of our Global Commodities operation, we
expect to realize the value of these contracts, as well as any contracts we may enter into in the future to manage our risk, over time as the contracts and related hedges settle in accordance with
their terms. Generally, we do not expect to realize the value of these contracts and related hedges by selling or assigning the contracts themselves in total. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Operating Expenses  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our merchant energy business operating expenses decreased $195.5&nbsp;million during 2009 as compared to 2008 due to lower performance-based labor
and benefit costs of $95.7&nbsp;million and lower non-labor operating expenses of $99.8&nbsp;million, part of which represents the absence of costs from the divestitures completed in
2009 and from deconsolidating CENG on November&nbsp;6, 2009. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our
merchant energy business operating expenses decreased $62.1&nbsp;million during 2008 compared to 2007 due to lower performance-based labor and benefit costs at our merchant energy
business of $129.2&nbsp;million, partially offset by higher non-labor operating expenses of $67.1&nbsp;million, which included approximately $32&nbsp;million of higher bad debt
expense. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
2010, we expect a further decrease in operating expenses as a result of the deconsolidation of CENG on November&nbsp;6, 2009. We discuss this impact further in the </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><I>Effects of Transaction with EDF on Statement of Income
(Loss)</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> section. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Merger Termination and Strategic Alternatives Costs  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>We discuss costs related to the terminated merger with MidAmerican, the conversion of our Series&nbsp;A Preferred Stock, our transaction with EDF
and our pursuit of other strategic alternatives in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;2 to Consolidated Financial Statements</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Impairment Losses and Other Costs  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our impairment losses and other costs are discussed in more detail in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;2 to Consolidated Financial
Statements</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Workforce Reduction Costs  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our merchant energy business recognized expenses associated with our workforce reduction efforts as discussed in more detail in </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;2 to Consolidated Financial Statements</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>.
</FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Amortization of Credit Facility Amendment Fees  </I></B></FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our merchant energy business incurred costs related to the amortization of credit facility amendment fees in connection with the EDF transaction.
These costs are classified as part of "Other income (expense)" in our Consolidated Statements of Income (Loss). </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Depreciation, Depletion and Amortization Expense  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our merchant energy business incurred lower depreciation, depletion and amortization expenses of $36.9&nbsp;million during 2009 compared to 2008
due to the absence of depletion expenses of $43.1&nbsp;million as a result of divestitures made in 2008 in our upstream gas operations, partially offset by an increase of $6.2&nbsp;million in
depreciation on our generating facilities. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Merchant
energy depreciation, depletion, and amortization expenses increased $17.2&nbsp;million in 2008 compared to 2007 mostly due to increased depletion expenses related to our
upstream natural gas operations as a result of increased drilling and production, partially offset by the cessation of operations at our synfuel facilities in December 2007. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Taxes Other Than Income Taxes  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Taxes other than income taxes decreased $15.8&nbsp;million in 2009 compared to 2008, due to $8.1&nbsp;million of lower gross receipts taxes at
our retail customer supply operation, $5.8&nbsp;million of lower production taxes related to our upstream gas producing properties, and $1.9&nbsp;million in lower property, franchise, and other
taxes. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Taxes
other than income taxes increased $14.1&nbsp;million in 2008 compared to 2007, due to $9.8&nbsp;million in higher property and franchise taxes at our Generation operation,
$2.9&nbsp;million of higher gross receipts taxes at our retail customer supply operation, and $1.4&nbsp;million of higher production taxes related to our upstream gas producing properties. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Gain on Sale of 49.99% Interest in CENG  </I></B></FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>On November&nbsp;6, 2009, we completed the sale of a 49.99% membership interest in CENG to EDF. As a result of this sale, we recognized a
$7.4&nbsp;billion pre-tax gain. We discuss this transaction in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;2 to Consolidated Financial Statements</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> (Loss) Gain on Divestitures  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>During 2009, we sold a majority of our international commodities operation, our Houston-based gas trading operation, certain other trading
operations, and a uranium market participant, and we recognized a pre-tax loss of $464.2&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
2008, we recognized net gains of $25.5&nbsp;million, including a $14.3&nbsp;million gain, net of the noncontrolling interest gain of $0.7&nbsp;million, related to the sale
of our working interests in oil and natural gas producing wells in Oklahoma to Constellation Energy Partners that was completed in the first quarter of 2008. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
discuss these divestitures in more detail in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;2 to Consolidated Financial Statements.</I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Equity Investment (Losses) Earnings  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>During 2009, our equity investment earnings decreased $63.6&nbsp;million from 2008 primarily due to $39.1&nbsp;million of lower earnings from our
shipping joint venture as a result of the sale of our interests in July 2009, $16.5&nbsp;million of lower earnings on investments in power projects, and $12.3&nbsp;million of lower earnings from
our investment in CEP, partially offset by $4.3&nbsp;million in earnings related to our investment in CENG. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Equity
investment earnings increased $74.2&nbsp;million in 2008 compared to 2007 primarily due to $38.0&nbsp;million of higher earnings from our shipping joint venture,
$34.6&nbsp;million of higher earnings on investments in power projects, and $1.6&nbsp;million of higher earnings from our investment in CEP. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> Regulated Electric Business  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our regulated electric business is discussed in detail in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Item&nbsp;1. Business&#151;Electric
Business</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> section. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2009, we distributed less electricity to residential customers due to decreased usage per customer, partially offset by colder winter weather and an increased
number of customers. We distributed less electricity to industrial customers primarily due to decreased usage per customer. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
2008, we distributed less electricity to residential and commercial customers due to milder weather and decreased usage per customer, partially offset by an increased number of
customers. We distributed less electricity to industrial customers primarily due to decreased usage per customer. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Residential Customer Rate Credit</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>On October&nbsp;30, 2009, the Maryland PSC issued an order approving Constellation Energy's transaction with EDF. Among other things, the order
required Constellation Energy to fund a one-time distribution rate credit for BGE residential customers before the end of March 2010 totaling $110.5&nbsp;million, or approximately $100
per customer, for which BGE recorded a liability in November 2009. In December 2009, BGE filed a tariff with the Maryland PSC stating BGE would give residential customers a rate credit of exactly $100
per customer. As a result, BGE accrued an additional $1.9&nbsp;million for a total fourth quarter 2009 accrual of $112.4&nbsp;million. The portion of this total credit allocated to residential
electric customers was $95.0&nbsp;million
pre-tax. This credit was accrued in the fourth quarter of 2009 and will be applied to BGE residential electric customer bills in the first quarter of 2010. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Nuclear Decommissioning Charges</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Effective January&nbsp;1, 2009, BGE and Calvert Cliffs Nuclear Power Plant&nbsp;Inc. (Calvert Cliffs) mutually agreed to terminate the
decommissioning funds collection agent agreement, which was effective from July&nbsp;1, 2000 to December&nbsp;31, 2008. As a result, BGE ceased transferring funds to provide for the
decommissioning of Calvert Cliffs Unit 1 and Unit 2. Calvert Cliffs retains the obligation to provide adequate assurances of funding pursuant to Nuclear Regulatory Commission requirements. Under the
2008&nbsp;Maryland settlement agreement, BGE will continue to provide certain credits to residential customers and assess certain charges to all customers relating to decommissioning. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Smart Energy Savers Program<SUP>SM</SUP> Surcharge</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Beginning in 2009, the Maryland PSC approved customer surcharges through which BGE recovers costs associated with certain programs designed to help
BGE manage peak demand and encourage customer energy conservation. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Maryland Settlement Credit</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>As discussed in more detail in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;2 to Consolidated Financial Statements</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>, BGE entered into a
settlement agreement with the State of Maryland and other parties, which provided residential electric customers a credit totaling $170 per customer. The estimated settlement of $188.2&nbsp;million
was accrued in the second quarter of 2008 and a total of $189.1&nbsp;million was credited to customers in the third and fourth quarters of 2008. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Revenue Decoupling</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The Maryland PSC has allowed us to record a monthly adjustment to our electric distribution revenues from residential and small commercial customers
since 2008 and for the majority of our large commercial and industrial customers since February 2009 to eliminate the effect of abnormal weather and usage patterns per customer on our electric
distribution volumes, thereby recovering a specified dollar amount of distribution revenues per customer, by customer class, regardless of changes in consumption levels. This means BGE recognizes
revenues at Maryland PSC-approved levels per customer, regardless of what actual distribution volumes were for a billing period. Therefore, while these revenues are affected by customer
growth, they will not be affected by actual weather or usage conditions. We then bill or credit impacted customers in subsequent months for the difference between approved revenue levels under revenue
decoupling and actual customer billings. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Standard Offer Service</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>BGE provides standard offer service for customers that do not select an alternative supplier. We discuss the provisions of Maryland's Senate Bill 1
related to residential electric rates in the </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Business Environment&#151;Regulation&#151;Maryland&#151;Senate Bills 1 and 400</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
section. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Standard
offer service revenues decreased in 2009 compared to 2008 mostly due to lower standard offer service volumes, partially offset by higher standard offer service rates. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Standard
offer service revenues increased in 2008 compared to 2007 mostly due to higher standard offer service rates, partially offset by lower standard offer service volumes. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Rate Stabilization Credits</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>As a result of Senate Bill 1, we were required to defer from July&nbsp;1, 2006 until May&nbsp;31, 2007 a portion of the full market rate increase
resulting from the expiration of the residential rate freeze. In addition, we offered a plan also required under Senate Bill 1 allowing residential customers the option to defer the transition to
market rates from June&nbsp;1, 2007 until January&nbsp;1, 2008. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenues
in 2008 increased compared to 2007 as a result of the expiration of the rate stabilization plans. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Rate Stabilization Recovery</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In late June 2007, BGE began recovering amounts deferred during the first rate deferral period that ended on May&nbsp;31, 2007. The recovery of the
first rate stabilization plan will occur over approximately ten years. In April 2008, BGE began recovering amounts deferred during the second rate deferral period that ended on December&nbsp;31,
2007. The recovery of the second rate deferral occurred over a 21-month period that began April&nbsp;1, 2008 and ended on December&nbsp;31, 2009. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Financing Credits</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Concurrent with the recovery of the deferred amounts related to the first rate deferral period, we are providing credits to residential customers to
compensate them primarily for income tax benefits associated with the financing of the deferred amounts with rate stabilization bonds. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Senate Bill 1 Credits</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>As a result of Senate Bill 1, beginning January&nbsp;1, 2007, we were required to provide to residential electric customers a credit equal to the
amount collected from all BGE electric customers for the decommissioning of our Calvert Cliffs Nuclear Power Plant and to suspend collection of the residential return component of the administrative
charge collected through residential SOS rates through May&nbsp;31, 2007. Under an order issued by the Maryland PSC in May 2007, as of June&nbsp;1, 2007, we were required to reinstate collection
of the residential return component of the administration charge in rates and to provide all residential electric customers a credit for the residential return component of the administrative charge.
Under the 2008&nbsp;Maryland settlement agreement, which is discussed in more detail in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;2 to Consolidated Financial Statements</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>, BGE was
allowed to resume collection of the residential return portion of the administrative charge from June&nbsp;1, 2008 through May&nbsp;31, 2010 without having to rebate it to residential customers. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
increase in revenues during 2009 compared to 2008 is primarily due to the absence of the credit for the residential return component of the administrative charge which was suspended
under the Maryland settlement agreement, partially offset by lower distribution volumes. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
increase in revenues during 2008 compared to 2007 is primarily due to the absence of the credit for the residential return component of the administrative charge which was suspended
under the Maryland settlement agreement, partially offset by lower distribution volumes. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Actual Costs</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>BGE's actual costs for electricity purchased for resale decreased $39.2&nbsp;million for 2009 compared to 2008, primarily due to lower standard
offer service volumes, partially offset by higher standard offer service rates. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;BGE's
actual costs for electricity purchased for resale increased $61.9&nbsp;million for 2008 compared to 2007, primarily due to higher contract prices to purchase electricity for our
customers, partially offset by lower volumes. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Deferral under Rate Stabilization Plan</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The deferral of the difference between our actual costs of electricity purchased for resale and what we are allowed to bill customers under Senate
Bill 1 ended on December&nbsp;31, 2007. In 2007, we deferred $287.3&nbsp;million in electricity purchased for resale expenses. These deferred expenses, plus carrying charges, are included in
"Regulatory Assets (net)" in our, and BGE's, Consolidated Balance Sheets. We discuss the provisions of Senate Bill 1 related to residential electric rates in the </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Business
Environment&#151;Regulation&#151;Maryland&#151;Senate Bills 1 and 400</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> section. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Recovery under Rate Stabilization Plans</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In late June 2007, we began recovering previously deferred amounts from customers. We recovered $59.0&nbsp;million per year in 2009 and 2008 in
deferred electricity purchased for resale expenses. These collections secure the payment of principal and interest and other ongoing costs associated with rate stabilization bonds issued by a
subsidiary of BGE in June 2007. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Electric Operations and Maintenance Expenses  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Regulated electric operations and maintenance expenses increased $18.5&nbsp;million in 2009 compared to 2008, primarily due to increased
uncollectible accounts receivable expense of $5.1&nbsp;million and the impact of inflation on other costs of $8.0&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Regulated
electric operations and maintenance expenses increased $4.4&nbsp;million in 2008 compared to 2007 mostly due to increased uncollectible accounts receivable expense of
$14.2&nbsp;million, partially offset by $9.0&nbsp;million of lower labor and benefit costs. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Workforce Reduction Costs  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>During the fourth quarter of 2008, we executed a restructuring of the workforce. We recognized a $4.6&nbsp;million pre-tax charge in
2008 related to this reduction in force. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
incurred no workforce reduction costs in 2009 or 2007. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Electric Depreciation and Amortization Expense  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Regulated electric depreciation and amortization expense increased $33.9&nbsp;million during 2009, compared to 2008, primarily due to
$43.3&nbsp;million in increased amortization expense associated with the Smart Energy Savers Program<SUP>SM</SUP> and additional property placed in service in 2009, partially offset by
$18.7&nbsp;million in lower depreciation expense as a result of revised depreciation rates which were implemented on June&nbsp;1, 2008 for regulatory and financial reporting purposes as part of
the Maryland settlement agreement. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Regulated
electric depreciation and amortization expense decreased $3.2&nbsp;million in 2008 compared to 2007, primarily due to $10.0&nbsp;million in lower depreciation expense as a
result of revised depreciation rates which were implemented on June&nbsp;1, 2008 for regulatory and financial reporting purposes as part of the Maryland settlement agreement. The Maryland settlement
agreement is discussed in more detail in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;2 to Consolidated Financial Statements</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. This decrease was partially offset by additional property
placed in service in 2008. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Taxes Other Than Income Taxes  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Taxes other than income taxes increased $3.8&nbsp;million during 2009 compared to 2008, primarily due to the impact of $94.1&nbsp;million
pre-tax in lower customer credits on franchise taxes. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> Regulated Gas Business  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Our regulated gas business is discussed in detail in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Item&nbsp;1. Business&#151;Gas
Business</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2> section. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2009, we distributed more gas to residential customers due to colder winter weather. We distributed less gas to commercial customers due to decreased usage per
customer, partially offset by an increased number of customers and colder weather. We distributed more gas to industrial customers mostly due to increased usage per customer, partially offset by a
decreased number of customers. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
2008, we distributed less gas to residential customers and commercial customers due to decreased usage per customer, partially offset by an increased number of customers. We
distributed more gas to industrial customers mostly due to increased usage per customer, partially offset by a decreased number of customers. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Residential Customer Rate Credit</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>On October&nbsp;30, 2009, the Maryland PSC issued an order approving Constellation Energy's transaction with EDF. Among other things, the order
required Constellation Energy to fund a one-time distribution rate credit for BGE residential customers totaling $110.5&nbsp;million, or approximately $100 per customer, for which BGE
recorded a liability in November 2009. In December 2009, BGE filed a tariff with the Maryland PSC stating BGE would give residential customers a rate credit of exactly $100 per customer. As a result,
BGE accrued an additional $1.9&nbsp;million for a total fourth quarter 2009 accrual of $112.4&nbsp;million. The portion of this total credit allocated to residential gas customers was
$17.4&nbsp;million pre-tax. This
credit was accrued in the fourth quarter of 2009 and will be applied to BGE residential gas customer bills in the first quarter of 2010. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Conservation Surcharge</U>  </I></FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Beginning February 2009, the Maryland PSC approved a customer surcharge through which BGE recovers costs associated with certain programs designed to
help BGE encourage customer conservation. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Gas Revenue Decoupling</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The Maryland PSC allows us to record a monthly adjustment to our gas distribution revenues to eliminate the effect of abnormal weather and usage
patterns per customer on our gas distribution volumes, thereby recovering a specified dollar amount of distribution revenues per customer, by customer class, regardless of changes in consumption
levels. This means BGE recognizes revenues at Maryland PSC-approved levels per customer, regardless of what actual distribution volumes were for a billing period. Therefore, while these
revenues are affected by customer growth, they will not be affected by actual weather or usage conditions. We then bill or credit impacted customers in subsequent months for the difference between
approved revenue levels under revenue decoupling and actual customer billings. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Gas Cost Adjustments</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>We charge our gas customers for the natural gas they purchase from us using gas cost adjustment clauses set by the Maryland PSC as described in </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;1 to Consolidated Financial Statements</I></FONT><FONT
SIZE=2>. However, under the market-based rates mechanism approved by the Maryland PSC, our actual cost of gas
is compared to a market index (a measure of the market price of gas in a given period). The difference between our actual cost and the market index is shared equally between shareholders and
customers. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Customers
who do not purchase gas from BGE are not subject to the gas cost adjustment clauses because we are not selling gas to them. However, these customers are charged base rates to
recover the costs BGE incurs to deliver their gas through our distribution system, and are included in the gas distribution volume revenues. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Gas
cost adjustment revenues decreased in 2009 compared to 2008 because we sold less gas at lower prices. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Gas
cost adjustment revenues increased in 2008 compared to 2007 because we sold gas at higher prices, partially offset by less gas sold. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> <U>Off-System Gas Sales</U>  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Off-system gas sales are low-margin direct sales of gas to wholesale suppliers of natural gas. Off-system gas
sales, which occur after BGE has satisfied its customers' demand, are not subject to gas cost adjustments. The Maryland PSC approved an arrangement for part of the margin from off-system
sales to benefit customers (through reduced costs) and the remainder to be retained by BGE (which benefits shareholders). Changes in off-system sales do not significantly impact earnings. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenues
from off-system gas sales decreased in 2009 compared to 2008 because we sold less gas at lower prices. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenues
from off-system gas sales increased in 2008 compared to 2007 because we sold gas at higher prices, partially offset by less gas sold. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Gas Purchased For Resale Expenses  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Gas purchased for resale expenses include the cost of gas purchased for resale to our customers and for off-system sales. These costs do
not include the cost of gas purchased by delivery service only customers. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Gas
costs decreased $244.6&nbsp;million in 2009 compared to 2008 because we purchased less gas at lower prices. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Gas
costs increased $54.7&nbsp;million in 2008 compared to 2007 because we purchased gas at higher prices, partially offset by lower volumes. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Gas Operations and Maintenance Expenses  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Regulated gas operation and maintenance expenses increased $3.6&nbsp;million during 2009 compared to 2008, primarily due to increased uncollectible
accounts receivable expense of $2.0&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Gas Workforce Reduction Costs  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>During the fourth quarter of 2008, we executed a restructuring of the workforce at our operations. We recognized a $1.8&nbsp;million
pre-tax charge in 2008 related to this reduction in force. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
incurred no workforce reduction costs in 2009 or 2007. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Gas Depreciation and Amortization  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Regulated gas depreciation and amortization expense decreased $3.1&nbsp;million in 2008 compared to 2007, primarily due to $3.5&nbsp;million in
lower depreciation expense as a result of revised depreciation rates which were implemented on June&nbsp;1, 2008 for regulatory and financial reporting purposes as part of the Maryland settlement
agreement. The Maryland settlement agreement is discussed in more detail in </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Note&nbsp;2 to Consolidated Financial Statements</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=1><I>Above amounts include intercompany transactions eliminated in our Consolidated Financial Statements. Note&nbsp;3
provides a reconciliation of operating results by segment to our Consolidated Financial Statements.</I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net loss attributable to common stock for 2009 exceeded net income attributable to common stock for 2008 by $33.7&nbsp;million primarily due to
increased equity losses from UNE of $11.4&nbsp;million after-tax, increased impairment losses and other costs due to an impairment of a district chilled water energy plant of $7.1&nbsp;million
after-tax and reduction for noncontrolling interest, a write-off of an uncollectible advance to an affiliate of $4.3&nbsp;million after-tax, and higher
depreciation and amortization expense of $5.2&nbsp;million after-tax as a result of increased property additions during 2008. UNE will become part of our generation reportable segment in 2010. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net
income attributable to common stock decreased $11.8&nbsp;million in 2008 compared to 2007 primarily because the first quarter of 2007 included a gain related to a sale of a leasing
arrangement that did not occur in 2008 and due to increased depreciation and amortization of $8.7&nbsp;million after-tax. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B> Consolidated Nonoperating Income and Expenses  </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Other (Expense) Income  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>In 2009, we had other expenses of $140.7&nbsp;million and, in 2008, we had other expenses of $69.5&nbsp;million. The $71.2&nbsp;million
increase in 2009 compared to 2008 is mostly due to higher credit facility costs, including amortization of amendment fees. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
2008, we had other expenses of $69.5&nbsp;million and, in 2007 we had other income of $157.4&nbsp;million. The $226.9&nbsp;million decrease in 2008 compared to 2007 is mostly
due to lower interest and investment income of $75&nbsp;million as a result of a lower average cash
balance of approximately $850&nbsp;million and an increase in other-than-temporary impairment charges related to our nuclear decommissioning trust fund assets of
$156.5&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Other
income at BGE decreased $4.2&nbsp;million in 2009 compared to 2008 primarily due to decreases in both interest and investment income of $4.2&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Other
income at BGE increased $2.7&nbsp;million in 2008 compared to 2007 primarily due to an increase in equity funds capitalized on increased construction work in progress in 2008. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Fixed Charges  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Fixed charges increased $56.7&nbsp;million in 2008 compared to 2007 mostly due to a higher level of interest expense associated with the new debt
issuances. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Fixed
charges at BGE increased $14.6&nbsp;million in 2008 compared to 2007 mostly due to a higher level of interest expense associated with the new debt issuances. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> Income Taxes  </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Income tax expense increased $3,065.1&nbsp;million during 2009 compared to 2008 mostly due to higher income before income taxes due to the
recognition of the $7.4&nbsp;billion pre-tax gain on closing the transaction to sell a 49.99% membership interest in CENG. Additionally, there was lower income before income taxes for 2008,
primarily due to approximately $1.2&nbsp;billion of non-tax deductible merger termination and strategic alternative costs. However, in 2009, certain of these costs became tax deductible
as a result of closing the EDF transaction and we recorded a tax benefit for these items in 2009. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;BGE's
income tax expense increased $43.1&nbsp;million during 2009, mostly due to higher pre-tax income. For 2008, BGE had a lower effective tax rate as a result of a
reduction in its 2008 taxable income due to the impact of certain provisions of the 2008&nbsp;Maryland settlement agreement, which increased the relative impact of the favorable permanent tax
adjustments on its effective tax rate. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our
income tax expense decreased $506.6&nbsp;million during 2008 compared to 2007 mostly due to a decrease in income before income taxes, which included approximately
$1.2&nbsp;billion of non-tax deductible merger termination and strategic alternatives costs, partially offset by the absence of synthetic fuel tax credits, which expired in 2007. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>58</FONT></P>
